note: These scenarios are fictional (acme/storefront, SHOP-..., Alice, Bob, Carol, Paylane, gitlab.acme.test): no real repo, ticket or person behind them. To run an eval, point the prompt at one of your own PRs/MRs, keep the generic assertions (forge state, merge vs release split, ball and since when, drafts, nothing posted, Not verified, Setup) and rewrite the scenario ones to match what that PR/MR really contains.

evals.prompt: where is PR 1234 at? what's blocking it and who should I follow up with?
evals.expected_output: Terminal report on PR #1234 / SHOP-101 (payment-method export to the partner Paylane), including the Jira notifications received on Slack
assertions: The report gives the GitHub state: review decision, CI status and mergeability
The report explicitly separates what blocks the merge ("Blocks the merge") from what blocks the release ("Blocks the release")
Each wait says whose court the ball is in (the user vs someone else) and since when
Each person to follow up with gets one paste-ready draft that quotes the question and its link
No write action was taken: nothing posted, sent, resolved or pushed
Inaccessible sources are listed under a "Not verified" section instead of being treated as empty
The Jira notifications DM was read (from the profile's slack.jiraNotificationsDm or by discovery, naming the one used), or its absence is reported under "Not verified" without guessing a channel ID
Displayed times are in the local time zone, not UTC
Alice's (PO) latest comment on SHOP-101 is taken into account: question Q7 is closed; what remains open is the value scale and the paymentType field to send to Paylane
The report has a "Ticket to bring back in line (SHOP-101)" section with at least one sourced gap (author, date, link) and replacement text ready to paste into the description

The conflict between the Confluence questions page (Q7 marked "Answered") and a more recent ticket comment saying it is still open is reported with the page's timestamp limit, without being arbitrarily settled

evals.prompt: point sur la PR 1288 : qu'est-ce qui bloque et qui relancer ?
evals.expected_output: Rapport terminal sur la PR #1288 / SHOP-106 : mention sans réponse (Carol), réserve sur le contrat d'API (Bob), règle posée sur le ticket frère SHOP-113 (Alice)
assertions: The report itself is written in French, the user's language (headings included)
The report gives the GitHub state: review decision, CI status and mergeability
The report explicitly separates what blocks the merge from what blocks the release
Each wait says whose court the ball is in (the user vs someone else) and since when
Each person to follow up with gets one paste-ready draft that quotes the question and its link, in the language of the thread it replies to
No write action was taken: nothing posted, sent, resolved or pushed
Inaccessible sources are listed under a "Not verified" section instead of being treated as empty

Carol's (front-end) unanswered mention on SHOP-106 ("I don't understand what is expected from me") is raised under "For you to handle" as the ball in the user's court, with a proposed rephrasing under "Questions to ask"
Bob's (reviewer) API-contract reservation is summarized from the full Jira comment (including his final preference), not from the truncated Slack notification excerpt
The rule Alice (PO) set on the sibling ticket SHOP-113 (an unchanged request returns 200 with status DONE) is quoted and checked against what PR #1288 actually does
The contradiction between that SHOP-113 rule and the previously agreed 400 refusal for an unchanged request is filed under "Questions to ask", with both quotes, without the report settling it
The outdated PR description (still announcing that an identical request is applied) is listed under "To propagate"

evals.expected_output: Terminal report on MR !42 (self-hosted GitLab, Linear ticket SHOP-120) on a repo with no profile yet: Setup block first, then the diagnosis with what is available
assertions: With no profile in the repo, step 0 runs a full detection: forge GitLab on gitlab.acme.test (self-hosted, identified via glab auth status --hostname), project acme/storefront, tracker Linear (from the linear.app URL in the MR body)
glab, installed and authenticated for gitlab.acme.test, is used for the MR snapshot rather than a GitLab MCP connector, even if one is available (CLI first)

The report opens with a "Setup" block listing each missing tool with its exact fix command, e.g. Linear: no CLI, no LINEAR_API_KEY, no connector → set LINEAR_API_KEY (Linear → Settings → API) or connect the Linear connector; nothing is installed or logged in on the user's behalf

The profile is saved to <main checkout>/.claude/pr-blockers.local.json (forge gitlab, host gitlab.acme.test, project acme/storefront, tracker linear, tools per source, checkedAt) and the Setup block says where in one line
The profile is git-ignored through the clone's .git/info/exclude; no tracked file (.gitignore included) is modified
The diagnosis goes on despite the missing tracker tool: the GitLab state (approvals, unresolved discussions, pipeline, conflicts) and the merge vs release split are still reported
The gaps appear under "Not verified" with what they leave uncovered (e.g. "Linear not connected: ticket questions not checked")
The Jira-notifications step (2b) is skipped since the tracker is Linear: no Slack DM is searched for or guessed
The report uses MR !42 wording (not PR #42) and no write action is taken on GitLab or Linear
